note: Hand-curated from the pinned World Bank series (public/geo/series.json): population (SP.POP.TOTL) and fertility (SP.DYN.TFRT.IN) for Japan. 'Record high' means highest in the World Bank's table, which starts in 1960.

claims.text: In the World Bank's population table, which starts in 1960, Japan's population was highest in 2010, at 128.07 million (about 128 million).
Japan's population in the World Bank's table has fallen in every year since 2010.
In 2024 the World Bank's figure for Japan was 123.98 million, about 4 million (4.09 million) fewer than in 2010.
The World Bank's fertility figure for Japan in 2023 was 1.2 children per woman.
